 Print TVS Motor's Venu Srinivasan, daughter Lakshmi file caveats amid family inheritance dispute CHENNAI: Lakshmi Venu, daughter of Venu Srinivasan (VS), has formally sought partition of the joint family assets of the VS branch of the larger TVS family, escalating a dispute over the division of family wealth. Her mother, Mallika Srinivasan, has backed her demand and called for an amicable settlement. Venu is yet to respond. A statement issued on Lakshmi's behalf said she had, in a partition notice to her father, called upon him, as head of the family, to facilitate what she describes as a fair and lawful division of assets. Mallika said efforts to resolve the matter amicably had failed to make meaningful and timely progress. The rift centres on the division of family wealth and business interests. Mallika and Lakshmi argue a March 2024 MoU did not settle the economic interests through a formal valuation and mutually agreed division. Entitled to rightful share in joint family property: Lakshmi
 VS maintains that the split was fair, with Lakshmi taking over Sundaram-Clayton and son Sudarshan Venu taking over the TVS Motor business. The dispute escalated after a boardroom confrontation at Sundaram-Clayton earlier this year and recently took a legal turn, with family members filing caveats in Chennai courts. While VS maintains that ownership and control have been divided, Mallika and Lakshmi say the division of family wealth remains unresolved. Lakshmi's claim is based on her interpretation of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, as amended in 2005. She claimed that she is entitled to her rightful share in the joint family property and has an independent right to seek its partition. It is also founded on the equal rights of daughters recognised under section 6 of the Act. The assets covered by her claim include interests held through the VS Trust and other holding entities, encompassing businesses and assets allocated to the Venu Srinivasan branch under the 2020 TVS family arrangement. These include interests in TVS Holdings, TVS Motor Company, TVS Credit Services and Sundaram-Clayton. Lakshmi contends that the 2020 arrangement involving the wider TVS family did not partition assets within her immediate family. She has also argued that the March 2024 memorandum of understanding, which covered brand usage, trademarks and non-compete obligations, did not constitute an economic settlement involving the valuation and division of family wealth.  She alleges that the concentration of beneficial interests in favour of her brother, Sudarshan Venu, has excluded her from her lawful entitlements. She views this as not only a breach of the law but also a breach of trust, maintaining that daughters' rights to joint family property cannot be overridden through unilateral decisions or corporate arrangements. Supporting her daughter's claim, Mallika said: "As a mother, to me, a son and daughter are equal in every respect. I do believe that Lakshmi has a legitimate share of the family assets, not unequal to that of Sudarshan." Mallika reiterated her preference for a negotiated resolution through transparent dialogue, with equity, clarity and amity. She expressed hope that the family could move forward with grace and dignity.
